#### 1. immunodeficiency, common variable, 10  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-844456, Reactome:R-HSA-9660826)

**Proposed mechanism:** MEFV (HGNC:7040) —DISRUPTS→ Inflammasome activation (GO:0032657); Inflammasome activation (GO:0032657) —LEADS_TO→ Fever (HP:0000822); NFKB2 (HGNC:7734) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP207); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP207) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent infections (HP:00114210); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP207) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal B cell differentiation (HP:0004340). Loss-of-function mutations in MEFV impair inflammasome activation, leading to fever. Loss-of-function mutations in NFKB2 disrupt the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, resulting in recurrent infections and abnormal B cell differentiation. The NF-kappaB signaling pathway is a common downstream effector that is dysregulated in both diseases, leading to shared inflammatory and immune defects.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in NFKB2 in individuals with Familial Mediterranean Fever or the absence of mutations in MEFV in individuals with Common Variable Immunodeficiency 10 would falsify this shared mechanism hypothesis. Furthermore, demonstrating that the NF-kappaB signaling pathway is not affected by MEFV mutations or that inflammasome activation is not affected by NFKB2 mutations would also falsify the proposed link. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NF-kappaB signaling in both Familial Mediterranean Fever and Common Variable Immunodeficiency 10 could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both conditions, potentially improving treatment outcomes for patients with inflammatory and immunodeficiency disorders.

#### 2. heme oxygenase 1 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.430)

**Proposed mechanism:** MEFV (HGNC:7029) —DISRUPTS→ Pyrin inflammasome activation and IL-1beta release; Pyrin inflammasome activation and IL-1beta release —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent fever and serositis (HP:0011087); HMOX1 (HGNC:4891) —DISRUPTS→ Heme (CHEBI:17907); Heme (CHEBI:17907) —DECREASES→ Biliverdin (CHEBI:17419); Heme (CHEBI:17907) —LEADS_TO→ Heme accumulation due to reduced degradation (HP:0030126); Heme (CHEBI:17907) —INCREASES→ Oxidative stress and inflammation; Oxidative stress and inflammation —INCREASES→ Recurrent fever and serositis (HP:0011087). Mutations in MEFV lead to aberrant pyrin inflammasome activation and IL-1beta release, causing recurrent fevers and serositis. Mutations in HMOX1 impair heme degradation, leading to heme accumulation, which in turn exacerbates oxidative stress and inflammation, contributing to similar inflammatory phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that heme accumulation in HMOX1 deficiency does not significantly impact inflammatory pathways, or that MEFV mutations do not lead to increased pro-inflammatory cytokine release. _(variant: rs747050453)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting heme metabolism or downstream inflammatory mediators could offer therapeutic strategies for both Familial Mediterranean Fever and Heme Oxygenase 1 Deficiency.

Both familial Mediterranean fever (MEFV mutations) and Muckle-Wells syndrome (NLRP3 mutations) converge on the aberrant activation of the inflammasome, leading to excessive IL-1beta production and subsequent autoinflammatory phenotypes. The shared convergence point is the dysregulated processing and release of IL-1beta.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that MEFV mutations do not impact pyrin inflammasome activation or that NLRP3 mutations do not lead to increased IL-1beta secretion in relevant cellular models would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing common variants in MEFV or NLRP3 that are not associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting IL-1beta with biologic therapies (e.g., anakinra, canakinumab) has shown efficacy in both familial Mediterranean fever and Muckle-Wells syndrome, validating the shared mechanistic link and highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway.
